title: From the camera, a tree has a broken silhouette and air in the crown
note: From the primary camera the crown must have a leaf silhouette with gaps and air in it, not a lump on a post.
intent: The construction check proves the tree is made of cards; this one proves the result is legible. What makes a crown read from twenty metres is an irregular outline, holes the sky shows through, and a visible trunk or branch structure carrying it. Give the crown a non-circular envelope (three or four card clusters of different sizes rather than one shell), let a few cards sit clear of the mass, and keep the trunk thick enough to be seen — a pale stick under a ball is the failure mode. Pair it with flora.leaf-cards: the scene check answers how it is built, this one answers what the judge sees.

check.ask: Do the trees in this frame read as trees — a leafy, broken crown silhouette with gaps and a visible trunk or branches — rather than smooth or faceted balls, boulders or lumps sitting on posts?
check.note: Flora, from the primary camera: the crown must have a leaf silhouette and air in it. Pair with foliage-is-cards; the scene check proves the construction, this one proves the read.

port: The vegetation facet frames one tree in its primary camera and looks at the still before it iterates on anything else.
